headline: Braves eliminate Phillies in Wild Card Series Game 3
recap: The Phillies' season ended Thursday night in Atlanta, a 6-2 loss to the Braves in the decisive Game 3 of the NL Wild Card Series. Michael Harris II's three-run homer in the bottom of the first put the Braves up 3-0, and Ozzie Albies' two-run shot in the fourth made it 5-0 before starter Aaron Nola, charged with all three runs on Harris' homer, was pulled after 1 2/3 innings. Philadelphia got on the board in the sixth when Alec Bohm's groundout scored Kyle Schwarber, with Bryce Harper advancing to third. Matt Olson answered with a solo homer in the seventh to make it 6-1, and Trea Turner's eighth-inning sacrifice fly, scoring Derek Hill, closed out the scoring. Grant Holmes got the win in relief; Nola took the loss.

Philadelphia finishes the season 88-74, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-winning Braves. The Phillies reached the postseason as a wild card and were eliminated 2-1 in the best-of-three Wild Card Series, falling in Game 3 after splitting the first two games, both played in Atlanta.
There is no next game: the Phillies' season is over. Atlanta advances in the NL playoffs while Philadelphia heads into the offseason.
